codeReview.summary: The cancel implementation fully satisfies VAL-SKEL-007 and all four sub-requirements: (i) Cancel() calls POST /api/agents/{id}/ask-stream/cancel via AgentAdapter.CancelAsk(); (ii) Cancel() cancels the per-stream child context, and TestAgentAskStreamRuntime_CancelCallsCancelEndpointAndCancelsContext asserts ctxErr == context.Canceled via errors.Is(); (iii) AgentAskUpdateCancelled maps to '⊘ cancelled' display in ApplyAskStreamUpdate, distinct from the '⚠ error' state; (iv) per-stream context isolation (streamCtx, streamCancel := context.WithCancel(rt.parentCtx)) enables Submit() to immediately create a fresh stream, verified by TestAgentAskStreamRuntime_RapidResubmitAfterCancelIsAccepted and TestCockpitScreen_AskStreamRapidResubmitAfterCancel. 5 tests all pass under -race. golangci-lint reports 0 issues on the new files.

issues.description: The Cancel() method uses a best-effort pattern for the cancel endpoint call: cancelCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(rt.parentCtx, 5*time.Second); _ = canceler.CancelAsk(cancelCtx, agentID); cancel(). Errors from CancelAsk are silently discarded. This is a reasonable design choice for cancel (primary mechanism is context cancellation), but if the cancel endpoint returns an error the caller of Cancel() has no way to know. The feature description does not require reporting cancel endpoint errors, so this is acceptable.

TestAgentAskStreamRuntime_CancelCallsCancelEndpointAndCancelsContext relies on a 100ms time.Sleep after Cancel() returns before asserting ctxErr. The source goroutine must write ctxErr before the test reads it, but there is no synchronization primitive (e.g., a notifychannel) guaranteeing this ordering. In practice, the goroutine has sufficient time to exit within 100ms, but a notify-based approach (e.g., sync.WaitGroup.Add(1) / Done()) would make the test deterministic rather than time-dependent.

TestCockpitScreen_AskStreamRapidResubmitAfterCancel uses time.Sleep(50ms) before calling Cancel() to ensure the stream is in-flight. This is a time-based approach rather than a deterministic wait-for-in-flight mechanism. Similarly, the re-submit test uses a 50ms sleep before the second Submit(). These are acceptable given the feature's own requirement (iv) specifies 'within 100ms of cancel' as the acceptance window, but deterministic synchronization would strengthen the tests.

summary: skel-cancel PASS. The Cancel() method correctly calls the cancel endpoint (POST /api/agents/{id}/ask-stream/cancel) and cancels the per-stream request context, with the test double asserting context.Canceled via errors.Is(). The cancelled state renders as '⊘ cancelled' (distinct from '⚠ error'). Per-stream context isolation via context.WithCancel(rt.parentCtx) enables a fresh Submit() within 100ms of Cancel(). All 5 new tests pass under -race. golangci-lint clean on new files. Code is idiomatic Go with proper interface abstractions (AgentAskCanceler, AgentAskStreamSource), mutex-guarded state, and bounded update channel.
